decisive_items: brownish macules on the hands and feet
multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum
response.rationale: The combined GI polyposis with pigmented macules points most strongly to Peutz-Jeghers syndrome among the supplied options. R1 explains polyposis but not the skin or nail findings; R4, R5, and R3 are nonspecific for malabsorptive diarrhea but do not explain the polyp and pigmentation pattern.

rejected.why: Diffuse colorectal polyps are suggestive of a polyposis syndrome but it does not account for the mucocutaneous pigmentation or onychodystrophy.
Celiac disease can cause diarrhea and nutritional deficiencies but would not explain diffuse GI polyposis or brownish macules on hands and feet.
Crohn's disease may produce diarrhea, weight loss, and duodenal changes but it lacks the pigmented skin lesions and colonic polyp pattern.
Autoimmune enteropathy could explain diarrhea and hypoproteinemia but not the hyperpigmentation, polyposis, or nail changes.
